name: Bondi to Coogee Walk
description: Sydney's most iconic coastal walk winding past dramatic cliffs, ocean pools, and golden beaches from Bondi to Coogee.
suggested_itinerary: Start at Bondi Beach, walk south via Tamarama and Bronte, pause at Clovelly, finish at Coogee for a swim and lunch.
who_its_best_for: Anyone who wants stunning ocean scenery without technical difficulty — great for tourists, casual walkers, and fitness walkers.
who_should_avoid: Dog owners (no dogs allowed), pram users on steeper sections, people with vertigo near cliff edges.

name: Spit to Manly Walk
public_transport: Excellent — ferry from Circular Quay to Manly
description: A classic Sydney harbour walk through native bushland with sweeping harbour and ocean views, finishing at the iconic Manly Beach.
suggested_itinerary: Take bus to Spit Bridge, walk north through Dobroyd Head and Arabanoo Lookout, descend to Manly and catch the ferry home.
who_its_best_for: Confident walkers who want a half-day adventure combining bush and harbour scenery.
who_should_avoid: Young children, those with limited mobility, pram users.

name: Lane Cove Riverside Walk
description: A gentle riverside loop through Lane Cove National Park, perfect for families, dog walkers, and those seeking a peaceful bush escape close to the city.
suggested_itinerary: Park at the national park entrance, follow the river downstream, cross at the footbridge, return along the opposite bank.
who_its_best_for: Dog owners, families with young children, casual walkers seeking easy accessible green space.
who_should_avoid: Those wanting ocean views or a challenging workout.

name: Grand Canyon Track
public_transport: Moderate — train to Blackheath, taxi/walk to trailhead
description: One of the Blue Mountains' most spectacular walks — descending through ancient canyon walls, fern-filled grottoes, and cascading waterfalls.
suggested_itinerary: Descend from Evans Lookout into the canyon, explore the creek bed and overhangs, climb out via Neates Glen and return along the ridgeline.
who_its_best_for: Walkers who want a dramatic natural experience without a full-day commitment.
who_should_avoid: Those with a fear of confined spaces, people with knee problems on steep descents.

name: Wentworth Falls Track
public_transport: Good — train to Wentworth Falls station
safety_notes: No swimming at top of falls
description: A stunning Blue Mountains circuit descending past the three-tiered Wentworth Falls into the Jamison Valley, with dramatic valley views throughout.
suggested_itinerary: Start at the Conservation Hut, follow the top trail to the falls lookout, descend the steep valley trail, swim at the base pools, and climb the National Pass back up.
who_its_best_for: Experienced and moderately fit walkers who want a dramatic waterfall and valley experience.
who_should_avoid: Beginners, families with young children, those with knee or hip problems.

name: Barrenjoey Lighthouse Walk
public_transport: Good — bus to Palm Beach terminus
parking: Palm Beach carpark (can be busy on weekends)
safety_notes: Can be windy at the top
description: A short but rewarding headland walk to Sydney's most northerly lighthouse, with breathtaking views over Pittwater, Broken Bay, and the Pacific Ocean.
what_to_bring: Layers for wind at the top
suggested_itinerary: Park at Palm Beach, walk along the beach to the headland, take the lighthouse track to the summit, and enjoy panoramic 360-degree views.
who_its_best_for: Anyone who wants a big-reward short walk — families, tourists, casual walkers.
who_should_avoid: Dog owners, those who need flat terrain throughout.

name: Figure Eight Pools Walk
best_time: Low tide only — check tide charts before going
start_point: Burning Palms Beach, Royal National Park
public_transport: Good — train to Otford, walk in
parking: Bundeena or Otford (entry fee to national park)
safety_notes: Rogue waves can be deadly on rock platforms
People have died here — take warnings seriously
description: Sydney's most spectacular geological wonder — natural figure-eight shaped rock pools carved into coastal platforms. Only accessible at low tide.
suggested_itinerary: Take the train to Otford, descend to Burning Palms Beach, walk south along the coast to the rock platforms at low tide, return the same way.
who_its_best_for: Adventurous walkers willing to check tides and follow all safety advice.
who_should_avoid: Families with children, anyone during high tide, anyone not comfortable on slippery rock platforms.

name: Manly Dam Walk
start_point: Manly Dam carpark, King Street Reserve
parking: Free carpark at King Street Reserve
description: A popular northern beaches loop circling the Manly Dam reservoir through native bushland — great for dogs, families, and a morning workout.
suggested_itinerary: Start at the King Street carpark, follow the dam wall, loop clockwise around the reservoir through the bushland trails.
who_its_best_for: Dog owners, families, fitness walkers wanting a local nature escape near Manly.
who_should_avoid: Those wanting ocean views, pram users.

name: Lake Parramatta Circuit
best_time: Any time — swimming permitted in summer
start_point: Lake Parramatta entrance, near North Rocks Rd
safety_notes: Check swimming conditions before entering water
description: A gentle lakeside circuit in Western Sydney's hidden gem — Lake Parramatta Reserve — with swimming, picnicking, and easy bush walking for the whole family.
suggested_itinerary: Enter from North Rocks Road, follow the sealed path around the lake, stop for a swim or picnic at the beach area, complete the loop.
who_its_best_for: Families, dog owners, wheelchair users, pram users — one of Sydney's most accessible outdoor areas.
who_should_avoid: Those seeking a challenge or dramatic coastal or mountain scenery.

name: Federation Cliff Walk
public_transport: Good — bus to Dover Heights and Bondi
safety_notes: Stay well back from cliff edges
description: A stunning coastal cliff-top walk from Dover Heights to Bondi with sweeping ocean views, dramatic sandstone headlands, and some of Sydney's best sunset spots.
suggested_itinerary: Take the bus to Dover Heights, walk south along the cliff tops via Mackenzies Point, descend to Bondi Beach for dinner.
who_its_best_for: Couples, casual walkers, photography enthusiasts, sunset chasers.
who_should_avoid: Dog owners, those with a fear of heights near cliff edges, pram users.
